title: Build live dashboards and animate explainers with Claude
summary: Dashboards (beta, paid plans) turn plain-language questions on connected data such as Snowflake and Salesforce into live charts, and clicking a number shows its query. Motion (beta, Team and Enterprise) builds animated explainers from prompts as editable code, downloadable as MP4. Docs, Slides, and Design are now out of beta on every plan including Free, and Claude Design has moved into Claude, with the old URL working until December 14.

title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
summary: Anthropic built Scion, an in-house version control system that replaces git for its monorepo, plus Antique, a code review tool; the migration took about 5 months. The server handles history, blame, commits, and merges while always-online clients fetch only needed data via sparse or virtualized checkouts, reporting about 200x less CPU and memory than old git mirrors, checkouts in seconds, and a 25% CI CPU capacity gain. Anthropic notes Scion is not a general git replacement, but its lessons may help git platforms handle agent-scale workloads as Claude's speed shifts the bottleneck to human-scale developer infrastructure.

title: How the Claude Code team does code review
summary: Claude writes about 90% of the Claude Code codebase, and review is layered: self-check, AI and security review on every PR, and human approval scaled to risk. Approval tiers (none, one, or two humans) are set by a classifier, though sensitive paths such as billing, the auto-updater, and CI always require a human. From June to September merged PRs more than doubled and the revert share fell over 40%, and the team argues the right question is which check best catches a given risk rather than whether a human read the code.

title: How Block orchestrates Claude Fable across thousands of pull requests
summary: In an interview, Block's Bradley Axen describes using Claude Fable 5 for company-wide code migrations, where Fable plans and directs Opus and Sonnet to edit files and run tests, with one migration yielding about 1,000 merged PRs. Safeguards include two-person human approval for merges to main and prod deploys, and Fable refuses to bypass that approval. Engineers shift toward designing migrations and reviewing agent behavior, and tiered models cut cost.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5
summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5), billed as its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model. It runs about 75% cheaper on average than Haiku 4.5 and is the first Haiku with an adjustable effort setting. It suits summaries, classification, and database queries, and works as a subagent alongside Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, with Box reporting +11 points at about half the latency.

title: Agent observability on the Claude Platform
summary: The Claude Platform now exports OpenTelemetry traces from Managed Agents, the Messages API, and SDKs in public beta. Managed Agents and the Messages API need a destination configured in the Claude Console, while SDKs export automatically, and traces cover agent turns, model calls, and tool use with latency, token counts, and IDs. It follows OTel GenAI semantic conventions and works with Grafana Cloud, Datadog, Langfuse, Honeycomb, and any OTLP endpoint, supporting debugging, turning production traces into evals, and tracking org token usage.
